title: Convertible Rear Seat Backrest Cover Removal and Installation
introduction:
The backrest cover uses several different attachments: edge J-clips, pin-type retainers and hook-and-loop strips bonded to the foam. I treat it like unfastening a fitted jacket: release each attachment before asking the fabric to move. Pulling harder can turn an upholstery job into a foam repair.

This procedure covers the convertible configurations listed below, including removal of the cushion and backrest needed to reach the cover. The illustrations distinguish the edge attachments from the strips beneath the upholstery; keep that distinction in mind during removal and refitting.

items.name: Convertible configuration
items.detail: Applies to the supplied convertible rear-seat configuration with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines.

items.name: Floor-fastener tightening
items.detail: Have suitable torque equipment ready. When reinstalling the backrest, tighten its floor fasteners to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm), as specified in [Rear Seat Backrest - Convertible](#/document/G1709034).

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged components. Failure to use this protection may result in serious personal injury. Review the applicable [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before starting.

items.name: Position the front seats before cushion work
items.detail: Keep everyone and all objects clear of the seat travel; never adjust the driver seat while the vehicle is moving. Move both front seats fully forward using their fitted controls. For manual seats, lift the bar beneath the front of the cushion, slide the seat forward, release the bar and rock the seat backward and forward to confirm that it locks. For power seats, move the outboard seat-control switch forward. If power is needed, bring the valid key inside and use the confirmed OFF-to-engine-off-ON sequence above without pressing either pedal. Once the seats are positioned, return any known ON state to OFF using the button with both pedals released; leave a state already OFF alone. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before releasing the rear cushion.

items.name: Keep structural joints clear
items.detail: WARNING: Follow every seat installation step and note carefully. Do not place objects between seat components and the vehicle body or inside any joint in the seat structure. Incorrect installation can impair seat operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect the cushion locking tabs
items.detail: NOTICE: Press the locking tabs at the front of the rear cushion inward before lifting the cushion from the floor. Lifting without releasing them can damage the tabs.

items.name: Keep restraints usable
items.detail: During installation of both the backrest and cushion, keep the safety-belt webbing untwisted and leave the belts and buckles accessible to the occupant.

edits.text: Remove the rear seat backrest before releasing its cover. Refer to: [Rear Seat Backrest - Convertible](#/document/G1709034) (501-10B Rear Seats, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: First move both front seats fully forward using the fitted controls and known-state power sequence in preparation. At the front edge of the rear cushion, press the locking tabs inward to release them from the floor, then lift the cushion free and remove it. Pulling upward before pressing the tabs can damage them; see [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168). With the cushion out, release the backrest floor fasteners at its lower outer corners. The upper hooked locking clips behind the backrest must be unlocked separately: pivot each clip inward, toward the backrest, out of engagement with its body catch before lifting. Once the clips are released, lift the backrest upward off its mounts and remove it.

edits.text: Unhook the backrest cover J-clips from the frame along the side edges and lower edge shown in the illustration.
edits.why: These hooked edge attachments hold the cover around the frame. I free the perimeter first so the fabric can move without dragging against an attachment that is still engaged.

edits.text: Release the pin-type retainers securing the carpet portion of the backrest cover to the frame, then fold the carpet forward.
edits.why: The illustration marks the carpet's attachment points. Folding this layer aside exposes the next part of the cover attachment sequence.

edits.text: Release the backrest cover pin-type retainers along the top of the backrest frame.
edits.why: The upper retainers are separate from the carpet retainers. Freeing them releases the cover's remaining attachment to the top of the frame.

edits.text: NOTICE: Separate the backrest cover carefully from the hook-and-loop strips. Pulling carelessly can tear the strips away from the seat backrest foam pad.
edits.why: The mating faces need to separate while the foam-side strips remain attached to the pad.

edits.text: Carefully separate the cover's hook-and-loop strips from their mating strips on the backrest foam, then remove the backrest cover.
edits.why: The highlighted strips follow the edges of the upholstered inset sections, with additional short runs beside the upper center area. Work at those mating faces rather than pulling the whole cover against the foam. The intended result is a free cover with the foam-side strips still in place.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order: fit the cover over the foam and reconnect its hook-and-loop strips, secure the top pin-type retainers, return the carpet to position and secure its pin-type retainers, then reconnect the edge J-clips. Reinstall the backrest and rear seat cushion.
edits.why: Lower the backrest onto its upper mounts and pivot the hooked locking clips into engagement with their body catches, then secure its lower floor fasteners to the torque in the preparation requirements. Refit the cushion by reversing its removal, engaging its floor attachments, then return the front seats from their fully forward positions. During both backrest and cushion installation, keep the belt webbing untwisted and the belts and buckles accessible. I check these before calling the upholstery finished: a tidy cover must leave the seat attachments and restraints correctly assembled. Restore the front seats using the same fitted controls: for manual seats, lift the front bar, slide to the required position, release and rock to confirm locking; for power seats, move the outboard switch backward as required with everyone and all objects clear. If power is needed, bring the key inside and select engine-off ON only from confirmed OFF, with both pedals released. After positioning, return known ON to OFF with the button and both pedals released; do not toggle a state already OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle. Keep the car parked and restrained throughout, and do not use a seat that is not securely retained.

editorialRevision.scope: Known-state parked preparation and actual manual/powered seat positioning/restoration; upper-backrest hooked clip pivot clarification using actual E187414 and prior independently approved same-source observation. Primary action text, cover attachment sequence, torque and warnings unchanged.
